ANNEX.text:
${P} SITE SURVEY: ADDENDUM, PRE-CONSTRUCTION
AUTHOR: ${c.lead}

The soil report keeps flagging the same anomaly at survey depth, dated eleven years before ground was even broken here.

Facilities insists it's a scanning error.

I have stopped asking why the error has a heartbeat.
ANNEX.title: SOIL REPORT

ARCHIVE.text:
${P} BLUEPRINT REVISION: LOG, PAGE 1

[A blueprint that depicts laboratory schematics shrouded by something organic-looking.]

[Sticky Note in the Margin]: "Do not disturb the center."

DRAFT NOTES: Internal review leads in circles. There are no further revisions on file. There are no originals on file, either. Whoever drew these up did not want credit.
 
— ${c.archivist}
ARCHIVE.title: DO NOT DISTURB

SERVER.text:
${P} EQUIPMENT DISCREPANCY REPORT

RACK #${WEEK}: No purchase order on file. No install ticket in the database. Serial number placards have been removed. Rack appears on the earliest floor plan we can find, which is dated before the slab was allegedly poured.
SERVER.title: Discrepancy Report

CLINIC.text:
${P} TISSUE SAMPLE #001:

Sample predates the clinic's commissioning by nine years. Chain of custody begins with a signature nobody can match to a living person.

The sample is not from an patient on record.

The sample is *from* the site.
CLINIC.title: Tissue Sample

CHASM.text:
${P} ARCHITECTURAL RESEARCH REPORT: "CHASM" ANCHORS

The catwalk anchors are drilled into a face that dates much older than the excavation project that supposedly exposed it.

Whatever cut out this void did it before anybody we know got here. All we did was find it, hang walkways in it, and then we wrote "excavation" on the invoice to cover the expenses.

- ${c.lead}
CHASM.title: Chasm Anchors

ANNEX.text:
INTERNAL SMTP SERVER REPORT: UNSENT MAIL

FROM: ${c.custodian}
TO: ${c.lead}
SUBJECT: RE: Supply Demands

Now that you mention it... ${c.lost} asked me for chalk last week. Not a pen, not a marker. Chalk.

I didn't think anything of it until I found the supply boxes empty.

It certainly would explain why we keep finding notes in chalk everywhere. Do you think it's ${c.lost}?
ANNEX.title: Unsent Mail

ARCHIVE.text:
SHELVING MEMO

We keep finding doors sealed from a side that has no handle.

${c.lost} filed the original blueprints personally. ${c.lost} is the only one who would know exactly how to open them.

- ${c.archivist}
ARCHIVE.title: Doors With No Handles

SERVER.text:
SECURITY BADGE AUDIT: SERVER RACK ROOM ACCESS

${c.lost}'s credentials are still cycling normally. They've had forty-one badge reads since they disappeared, all from the inside face of doors we have logged as sealed.

It would be impossible for the credentials to be cloned; they are biologically linked to ${c.lost}.

That badge is being used and carried by ${c.lost}.

Or something in ${c.lost}'s body.

- ${c.custodian}
SERVER.title: Server Access

CLINIC.text:
STOCK TAKE: CLINIC WARD STORAGE

Gauze, water and ration bars run short on a consistent and weekly cycle that nobody has authorized.

Nothing else moves or changes.

Whoever is taking inventory is taking exactly what one person needs and is being careful not to be greedy about it.
CLINIC.title: Stock Take

CHASM.text:
NOTE: CATWALK ACCESS PLATE

Plate 6 was cut open from the underside and bolted shut again from the underside, which would have required somebody to be down there when it closed and to still be down there to close it.

The bolts are hand-tightened, which means whoever did it expects to come back through here eventually.
CHASM.title: Catwalk

ANNEX.text:
IT BULLETIN #${ctx.seed}
FROM: FACILITY MANAGEMENT

Outbound network traffic spiked again last night. Staff were given strict orders to log off an go home.

Nobody was logged in last night, but the outbound packets are personnel files.

Ours.

- (${c.custodian})
ANNEX.title: Traffic Spike

ARCHIVE.text:
REQUISITION TICKET #${ctx.seed}

REQUESTED: Explanation for the antenna array logged under "HVAC."

VERDICT: DENIED

REASON: We assure you, the array is HVAC-related equipment. It regulates the temperature of *something*. That much we know. We were just never told what, exactly.

We don't want to know. Neither should you.

Please stop asking.
 
— ${c.archivist}
ARCHIVE.title: HVAC

SERVER.title: Inventory Packet

CLINIC.text:
AUDIOLOGY REPORT #${ctx.seed}: FINAL ENTRY

The tone of the hum is amplitude modulated. I plotted six hours of it against the personnel index and the peaks land on the roll call. It is not a symptom, either. It is the purpose.

It is a manifest, and we are being read out on it like a list to be tallied.
CLINIC.title: Audiology Report

CHASM.text:
ANTENNA ARRAY SURVEY

What the drawings call structural bracing across the chasm face is actually an array of phased elements, correctly spaced for the carrier frequency, aimed up the shaft and out.

The building has an antenna and we hung catwalks and search lights off of it.

Idiots.

- ${c.custodian}
CHASM.title: Array Survey
